analysis.title: Weekly Pulse: Focus on income in global sectors (Amundi ETF, 13 November 2026)
key_insights: Dispersion of MSCI World sector returns reached a multi-year high in 2026. The monthly gap between the best and worst sector averaged 17.3pp year-to-date, against 9.2pp in 2024 and 11.9pp in 2022.

Monthly dispersion peaked at 22.0pp in March and 26.3pp in October, the highest readings of the past decade. Amundi attributes this to Middle East geopolitical tension, AI capex concerns and uncertainty over the inflation path.
Amundi reads the sustained dispersion as a possible regime shift rather than isolated spikes. In 2022 a rotation out of IT into energy and value caused a short-lived spike that then normalised.
Energy and communication services had the sharpest reversals of the year, alternating between leading and lagging month to month.

In a prolonged high-dispersion regime, broad index exposure could be penalised because underperforming sectors can outweigh diversification benefits. Amundi suggests an agile, selective sector allocation.
Amundi flags utilities and financials as sectors to watch. Both yield above 2.5%, well ahead of information technology, which gives income independent of price appreciation.
Forward P/E is 15.4x for financials and 20.0x for utilities, which Amundi calls reasonably valued.

Defensive, income-oriented sectors have outperformed quarter to date, while higher-multiple growth-sensitive exposures have faced headwinds. Amundi asks whether this is a transient repositioning or the start of a lasting leadership change.
Financials and banks UCITS ETFs took in close to EUR 1.0bn of net new assets since the start of November, after EUR -2.3bn of outflows year to date.

S&P World weighted and screened sector indices show a 3Y return correlation of about 98% with their parent indices. They target a minimum 30% cut in greenhouse gas intensity (scope 1 and 2) and a higher S&P Global ESG score than the parent index.
Weekly market summary: sticky US inflation data renewed bond market concern and unsettled expectations for the policy rate path. Global equities recovered, led by Japan and Europe.
Weekly UCITS ETF flows (5-11 Nov) went mostly to equities with a strong preference for US exposures. Fixed income flows were muted overall, with positive flows into EUR corporate debt.
Next week's market focus is Nvidia earnings (Tuesday), Anthropic's IPO and the FOMC minutes (Wednesday).

Dividend yield above 2.5%, forward P/E of 15.4x, and structural earnings growth prospects. ETF inflows of close to EUR 1.0bn since the start of November.
Dividend yield is well below utilities and financials. Higher-multiple growth-sensitive exposures have faced headwinds quarter to date.

earnings_insights: Nvidia earnings are due Tuesday 17 November 2026 and are named as a market focus for the week of 16-20 November. The report gives no estimates.

tension_points.bull_case: Defensive, income-oriented sectors such as utilities and financials have outperformed. They offer yields above 2.5% and forward P/Es of 15.4x and 20.0x, with structural earnings growth prospects.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher-multiple growth-sensitive exposures face headwinds from macro uncertainty, AI capex concerns and inflation path uncertainty. Amundi also says the rotation may be only a transient repositioning.

theme_stances.key_argument: Sector dispersion in 2026 is at a multi-year high and has been sustained, which may signal a regime shift that favours selective sector allocation over broad index exposure.
Utilities and financials combine yields above 2.5%, reasonable valuations and structural earnings growth prospects.
theme_stances.evidence: utilities and financials may be two industries worth a closer watch
